needs: buffer (owned output, push, drop by caller)
multi-way table lookups without arrays (if-chains or a lookup fn)
pitfalls: from_roman accepting loose numerals (IIII, VX, IC, MMMM, CDC, IXI) because the letter values add up to something in range
subtractive pair validation: only IV IX XL XC CD CM; IL, IC, XM, VX must fail
repetition limits: 3 for I X C M, 1 for V L D
rejecting values > 3999 (MMMM) and the empty string
non-ASCII/other bytes and lower case must be Err, never a panic or out-of-bounds index
buffer ownership: the Ok Buffer is heap-owned
difficulty_notes: Target L2. Two independent units, no state. to_roman is a standard greedy table; the discriminating part is from_roman canonicality. Reference validates by comparing the text against the on-the-fly re-encoding of the parsed value (no heap needed, so from_roman stays pure). Oracle: 192 to_roman cases (1..40, boundaries, samples across the range, 7 out-of-range), 246 from_roman (canonical samples + 59 invalid strings), plus one exhaustive round trip over all 3999 values counted as one case. Plan examples overlap the oracle on a few canonical values (1, 4, 14, 1994, 3999, XIV, MCMXCIV, MMMCMXCIX) and a few invalid strings (IIII, VX, MMMM, empty, ' X', 'XIV ', VV, IXI); the rest of the 59 invalid strings are hidden.
